findings.fix: Preserve according-to-flesh manner of warfare versus Ephesians' against-flesh opponents; do not merge the two relations.
findings.before: Both distinguish the conflict of Christian ministry from warfare against flesh. Ephesians names spiritual powers rather than blood and flesh; Corinthians distinguishes living in flesh from waging war according to flesh.
findings.after: Both describe Christian conflict using flesh language, but the constructions differ. Ephesians identifies spiritual powers as opponents instead of blood and flesh; Corinthians distinguishes walking in flesh from waging war according to flesh. Manner of warfare and its opponents are not made the same claim.
findings.resolution: Applied after complete independent reading of the actual source,target,context and rationale; no relationship,target IDs or source outcome changed.

findings.fix: Preserve the sword of the Spirit identified as the word of God, rather than relabeling it the Spirit's word.
findings.before: Both use God-enabled military equipment as a metaphor for spiritual action. Ephesians names truth, righteousness, gospel readiness, faith, salvation and the Spirit's word; Corinthians calls the weapons powerful through God and identifies arguments as what is pulled down.
findings.after: Both use God-enabled military equipment as a metaphor for spiritual action. Ephesians names truth, righteousness, gospel readiness, faith, salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God; Corinthians calls the weapons powerful through God and identifies arguments as what is pulled down.
findings.resolution: Applied after complete independent reading of the actual source,target,context and rationale; no relationship,target IDs or source outcome changed.

findings.fix: Distinguish an unwanted appearance of terrifying readers from the stated purpose of the writing in2:4.
findings.before: Both explain the intended effect of Paul's letters by rejecting a damaging purpose. The earlier letter was written through anguish and tears to communicate abundant love rather than make them sorrowful; the present statement rejects an appearance of terrifying them through letters.
findings.after: In2:4 the writer says he wrote through tears and anguish so the readers might know his abundant love, rather than to make them sorrowful; here he does not want to seem to terrify them through letters. The concern for letters' effects is shared while purpose and appearance remain distinct.
findings.resolution: Applied after complete independent reading of the actual source,target,context and rationale; no relationship,target IDs or source outcome changed.

findings.fix: Preserve even-if untrained speech as a qualified description rather than an unqualified factual admission.
findings.before: Both distinguish rhetorical impressiveness from the substance of Paul's ministry. The earlier letter denies lofty speech or wisdom while proclaiming God's mystery; here Paul concedes being untrained in speech but denies being deficient in knowledge.
findings.after: Both distinguish rhetorical presentation from the substance of Paul's ministry. The earlier letter says he did not come with lofty speech or wisdom when proclaiming God's mystery; here Paul says that even if untrained in speech, he is not untrained in knowledge. The conditional wording remains intact.
findings.resolution: Applied after complete independent reading of the actual source,target,context and rationale; no relationship,target IDs or source outcome changed.

findings.fix: Keep the actual and wording for two witnesses and three rather than replacing it with the familiar or label.
findings.before: The two-or-three-witness rule is explicitly quoted from Deuteronomy's requirement for establishing a matter. Deuteronomy also rejects a single witness. The third proposed visit is a different statement and is not converted into a count of witnesses.
findings.after: The witness wording closely matches Deuteronomy's requirement for establishing a matter: at the mouth of two witnesses and at the mouth of three. Deuteronomy also rejects a single witness. The third proposed visit is a different statement and is not converted into a count of witnesses.
findings.resolution: Applied after complete independent source/target/rationale comparison; no pair, identity, relationship or outcome changed.

findings.fix: The hope concerns the recipients knowing that we do not fail, rather than uncertainty about whether the speakers pass.
findings.before: The speakers' hope that they do not fail the test echoes the preceding command that the recipients test themselves. The change from you to we is preserved rather than assigning both statements automatically to the same group.
findings.after: The writer hopes the recipients will know that the speakers do not fail the test, after asking the recipients to test themselves. The change from you to we and the hoped-for recognition are preserved rather than turning both statements into one group's uncertain result.
findings.resolution: Applied after complete independent source/target/rationale comparison; no pair, identity, relationship or outcome changed.
